drinks.name: Espresso
drinks.header: A concentrated shot with a rich, golden crema.

difficulty.reason: Dialing in grind and pulling a balanced shot take practice.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

recipe.waterGuidance: Fill the machine reservoir; target 36 g of brewed espresso rather than measuring water into the portafilter.
steps: Grind 18 g of coffee finely and dose it into the portafilter.
Distribute, tamp evenly, and lock in the portafilter.
Set the machine to about 93°C and pull about 36 g of espresso in 25–30 seconds. Taste and adjust the grind next time.

drinks.name: Latte
drinks.header: Espresso softened with plenty of silky steamed milk.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and controlled milk steaming.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and pour it into a cup.
Steam 180 mL of milk to about 60°C, creating glossy microfoam.
Pour the milk into the espresso, finishing with a thin layer of foam.

drinks.name: Cappuccino
drinks.header: A balanced espresso and milk drink with a generous foam cap.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and a generous, even milk foam.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and pour it into a cup.
Steam 120 mL of milk to about 60°C, adding more air than for a latte.
Pour the milk over the espresso, keeping a generous foam layer on top.

drinks.name: Pour-over
drinks.header: A clear, flavorful cup made by slowly pouring water over coffee.

difficulty.reason: Requires a steady pour and attention to brew time.

caffeine.note: Approximate range centered on measured V60 servings; the result depends on bean and brew strength.

steps: Rinse the filter and add 20 g of medium-fine coffee.
Pour 40 mL of 94°C water to wet all the grounds; wait 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining 280 mL slowly in circles. Aim to finish draining in 3–4 minutes.

drinks.name: French press
drinks.header: An easy immersion brew with a rounded, heavier body.

difficulty.reason: Immersion brewing needs only a timed steep and careful pressing.

caffeine.note: Broad estimate informed by measured French press servings; this recipe's larger serving and bean choice change the result.

steps: Add 30 g of coarse coffee to the press and pour in 450 mL of 94°C water.
Stir gently, cover, and steep for 4 minutes.
Press the plunger slowly and pour right away.

drinks.name: Americano
drinks.header: Espresso lengthened with hot water for a gentler cup.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot followed by controlled dilution.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe.
Add 120–180 mL of water at about 85°C to a mug.
Pour the espresso into the water and adjust within the stated range to taste.

drinks.name: Macchiato
drinks.header: A traditional espresso marked with a small spoonful of milk foam.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and a small amount of textured milk foam.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Prepare the full double-shot Espresso recipe in a small cup.
Steam a little milk to about 60°C and spoon 5–10 mL of foam on top.

drinks.name: Turkish coffee
drinks.header: Finely ground coffee simmered in a cezve and served unfiltered.

difficulty.reason: Slow heating and watching the rising foam prevent boiling over.

caffeine.note: Approximate range around a measured 129.6 mg per 100 mL Turkish coffee result, scaled to a 70 mL serving; preparation varies.

steps: Add 70 mL of room-temperature water, 7 g of extra-fine coffee, and optional sugar to a cezve. Stir before heating.
Heat slowly until the foam rises; remove before it boils over.
Pour gently into a small cup and let the grounds settle before sipping.

drinks.name: Mocha
drinks.header: A comforting latte with chocolate blended in.

difficulty.reason: Requires espresso, chocolate mixing, and controlled milk steaming.

caffeine.note: Espresso-based estimate; 20 g of chocolate sauce may add a small, variable amount of caffeine.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe and stir 20 g of chocolate sauce into it until smooth.
Steam 180 mL of milk to about 60°C and pour it over the chocolate espresso.
Stir gently and serve.

drinks.name: Flat white
drinks.header: A small milk drink where the espresso stays prominent.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and fine, lightly aerated milk.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Prepare the Espresso recipe in a small cup.
Steam 140–160 mL of milk to about 60°C with very fine microfoam.
Pour the milk into the espresso with only a thin foam layer.

drinks.name: Iced latte
drinks.header: Fresh espresso poured over cold milk and ice.

difficulty.reason: Requires an espresso shot and simple cold assembly.

caffeine.note: Indicative range from measured espresso servings; bean, dose, and extraction can change the result.

steps: Fill a tall glass with 120 g of ice and add 180 mL of refrigerated milk.
Prepare the Espresso recipe.
Pour the espresso over the milk and ice; stir to combine.
